Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 3 days of frequent watery diarrhea (6–7/day), intermittent left lower abdominal cramping, initial vomiting and subjective fever at onset, now tolerating fluids; likely acute gastroenteritis after recent takeaway meal; conservative management advised with oral rehydration, paracetamol, rest, and follow-up if not improving in 3–4 days.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of loose, watery stools with increased frequency, associated intermittent crampy pain in the left lower abdomen, weakness/shakiness, and reduced appetite.
- Timeline:
  - 4 days ago: Ate Chinese restaurant takeaway with friends.
  - 3 days ago: Onset of symptoms (diarrhea, abdominal cramps, initial vomiting, felt hot/subjective fever).
  - Currently: Diarrhea ongoing 6–7 times/day; vomiting has stopped; feels weak/shaky; able to keep down fluids; eating mainly soups/smoothies/light foods.
- Character of symptoms:
  - Diarrhea: Watery/loose, 6–7/day; no blood reported.
  - Abdominal pain: Left lower quadrant, cramp-like, intermittent; no radiation to back.
  - Systemic: Felt hot at symptom onset; no measured temperature reported; currently no stated fever. Weak/shaky. Loss of appetite.
  - Vomiting: Occurred at symptom onset; no blood; now resolved.
- Triggers/exposures: Recent takeaway/Chinese restaurant 4 days prior. Household: one child vomited but no diarrhea; no similar symptoms in others.
- Impact on activities: Needs proximity to toilet; has continued working as an accountant but with difficulty.
- Pertinent negatives: No blood in stool; no back radiation; denies other chronic bowel issues.
- Medications tried: None reported prior to consult.
- Systems review: As above; no additional ROS documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma: Patient reports well-controlled; uses an inhaler (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented). No other chronic conditions reported.
- No prior gastrointestinal or bowel disorders reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Accountant; continued to attend work during illness.
- Living situation: Lives with wife and two children.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Does not drink alcohol.
- Recent dining out: Chinese restaurant 4 days prior.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Potential future: Stool testing if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days (discussed).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral; possible bacterial etiology discussed)
  - Assessment: 3 days watery diarrhea, left lower abdominal cramps, initial vomiting and subjective fever; exposure to restaurant meal; no blood in stool; able to tolerate fluids. No red flags documented.
  - Plan:
    - Conservative management and hydration emphasized.
    - Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) recommended (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Paracetamol for feverish feelings/aches: “two tablets up to four times a day” for a few days; tablet strength and route not documented.
    - Rest and take 2–3 days off work.
    - No antibiotics indicated at this time.
    - Follow-up if no improvement within 3–4 days for reassessment and possible stool testing.
- Issue 2: Risk of dehydration due to ongoing diarrhea
  - Plan:
    - Maintain adequate oral fluid intake; use oral rehydration salts as above.
    - Monitor symptoms; seek reassessment if unable to maintain hydration or if worsening (guidance to return if not improving given).
- Issue 3: Asthma—stable by history
  - Assessment: Well-controlled per patient; uses inhaler.
  - Plan: No changes discussed.

General plan items:
- Return/seek care if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days for further evaluation including stool studies.
- Rest and temporary work absence advised for 2–3 days.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Asthma inhaler name, dose, route, frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol tablet strength and route not documented; oral rehydration dosing not documented.
  - Vitals and physical examination not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Vomiting: Initially answered “no,” then reported vomiting at symptom onset now resolved (conflict noted).
  - Fever: Patient reports feeling hot/subjective fever at onset; no measured temperature and currently no stated fever; clinician recap included “fever” (subjective vs. measured—conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational overlaps; no major inaudible sections.
